_comment: Community-GGUF import matrix (A3). See PLAN.md 'Ecosystem-compat + input-parsing hardening'.
WHY: we test our own cstr/* conversions, not the ecosystem's. Issue #33 was exactly that gap —
the registry ships nomic-embed-text-v2-moe pointing at cstr/ GGUFs (which loaded), while the
community GGUF users actually reach for first (nomic-ai/*-GGUF, a llama.cpp export) aborted with
'missing required tensor attn.q.weight'. Nothing caught it before a user did.
Each entry pins a THIRD-PARTY GGUF of a model we claim to support. The driver asserts it loads,
reports the expected arch/dims, and produces a semantically sane embedding (the garbage guard —
a model loaded with fabricated hparams still emits floats, so dim+rc alone prove nothing).
Fields:
name          test id
repo/file     HuggingFace repo + filename of the COMMUNITY gguf
arch          expected general.architecture (documents which key family it exercises)
dim           expected embedding dimension — the silent-default trap (#33 would give 384)
n_layer       expected layer count (nomic: 12; the silent default is 6)
query_prefix / doc_prefix  task prefixes this model family requires
min_margin    cos(query, related) must exceed cos(query, unrelated) by at least this
ref_file      optional: our own conversion of the SAME model, for a cross-conversion A/B
min_ref_cos   optional: required cosine between the two conversions

MEASURED (2026-07-16, q4_k GGUF vs HF fp32, tests/hf_parity_community.py): bge-small 0.9962 | MiniLM 0.9919 | nomic-v2-moe 0.9797 | nomic-v1.5 0.9515. min_hf_cos=0.95 is sized to sit under the q4_k floor while still catching a structural bug (wrong pooling/rope/dims), which craters cosine far below it.

PRECISION CONTROL — the only way to tell 'quant floor' from 'our bug': re-run the SAME code path at f16/f32. bge-small f32 and nomic-v1.5 f16 both give per-stage cos=1.000000 vs HF at EVERY layer, proving both encoder paths (bert split-QKV/abs-pos AND nomic-bert fused-QKV/RoPE) are exact and every q4_k delta is quantization. Do this before ever calling a low cosine a bug.

control_file / control_min_cos: a HIGHER-PRECISION GGUF (f16/f32) of the SAME model. tests/prove_quant_control.py runs it per-stage vs the HF fp32 reference; ~1.0 at every layer proves the encoder GRAPH is exact, so the shipped-quant gap (measured_hf_cos) is quantization, NOT our bug. This automates the manual f16/f32 control that separated 'quant floor' from 'our bug' for #33.

models.name: nomic-embed-text-v2-moe
models.query: how do I bake sourdough bread
models.related: A step-by-step guide to baking sourdough loaves at home.
models.unrelated: The 1998 amendment to the municipal zoning ordinance.
models.notes: Regression guard for issue #33: llama.cpp export uses fused attn_qkv + ffn_*_exps tensors and nomic-bert-moe.* hparam keys. Before the fix this aborted at load; with hparams missing it would have run at 384-dim/6-layer.
models.measured_note: q4_k floor; f32/f16 control not run for this one (500MB+ HF model)

models.name: nomic-embed-text-v1.5
models.query: how do I bake sourdough bread
models.related: A step-by-step guide to baking sourdough loaves at home.
models.unrelated: The 1998 amendment to the municipal zoning ordinance.
models.notes: A THIRD arch string ('nomic-bert', distinct from nomic-bert-moe) — resolved by A2's arch-derived lookup with no new code. Guards a real latent bug: this GGUF declares nomic-bert.rope.freq_base=1000, but the pre-A2 loader read only bert.rope_theta and silently defaulted to 10000. Tensors resolve (fused attn_qkv), so it loaded, exited 0 and emitted a 768-dim vector — just a subtly wrong one. Effect is length-dependent: vs our cstr conversion (which also uses theta=1000), correct-vs-default cosine is a wash on a short query (0.9531 vs 0.9563, noise) but clearly better on long text (0.9435 vs 0.9278). That is exactly why rc+dim checks cannot catch it and the garbage guard/parity must.
models.measured_note: LOWEST of the matrix, and it is NOT a bug: per-stage f16 vs HF fp32 is cos=1.000000 at ALL 12 layers (norms identical), so the nomic-bert graph (fused QKV + RoPE) is exact. The q4_k drop is real but purely quantization, concentrated in the LAST block (layer_10 0.9977 -> layer_11 0.9499 — a step, not smooth drift). This model's final layer is unusually quant-sensitive; prefer f16/q8 for retrieval quality.

models.related: A step-by-step guide to baking sourdough loaves at home.

models.notes: Plain bert arch with SPLIT attn_q/k/v and absolute position embeddings — the opposite shape to the nomic entries, so the matrix covers both. Exercises pooling_type=2 (CLS), which maps to CrispEmbed pool_method=1; a mis-mapped pooling would still return a 384-dim vector, so only the garbage guard catches it.
models.measured_note: per-stage f32 vs HF fp32 is cos=1.000000 at ALL 12 layers — the bert path (split QKV + absolute positions) is exact; all q4_k deltas are quantization

models.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
models.query: how do I bake sourdough bread
models.related: A step-by-step guide to baking sourdough loaves at home.
models.unrelated: The 1998 amendment to the municipal zoning ordinance.
models.notes: The one entry with a cross-conversion A/B: a community Q4_K_M vs our own cstr iq4_xs of the same model. min_ref_cos is deliberately loose (0.90) — the two differ in quant AND converter, so this gates 'same model' agreement, not bit-parity. NOTE its dim/n_layer (384/6) coincide with the loader's silent defaults, so for THIS entry the shape check proves little and the garbage guard carries the weight.
models.measured_note: q4_k floor; per-stage profile is smooth monotonic decay 0.9994 -> 0.9897, no step-change

models.name: gte-modernbert-base
models.query: how do I bake sourdough bread
models.related: A step-by-step guide to baking sourdough loaves at home.
models.unrelated: The 1998 amendment to the municipal zoning ordinance.
models.notes: The FIRST modern-bert arch entry, and the one that proved community-BPE-encoder support is deeper than a #33 alias add. This llama.cpp export uses gpt2 byte-level BPE with merges in the tokenizer.ggml.merges KV ARRAY (not our tokenizer.merges tensor) and NO numeric tokenizer.ggml.type — only tokenizer.ggml.model='gpt2' + tokenizer.ggml.pre='modern-bert'. Before the fix the dispatch fell back to WordPiece (50368 vocab < the 100K SPM heuristic), tokenizing 'hello world' to the WRONG ids and emitting garbage (structural-gate emb_ln_out cos=0.58, cos(related) < cos(unrelated)). The fix: model-string-authoritative tokenizer dispatch, BPE merges from the KV array, the GPT-2 ByteLevel regex pre-tokenizer, plus loader aliases (attn_norm->ln1, ffn_norm->ln2, output_norm->final_norm, GeGLU-by-shape reroute of the fused ffn_up [H,2*inter]) and metadata (pre_ln, inverted dual RoPE theta: freq_base=global/160000, freq_base_swa=local/10000, sliding_window->local window, sliding_window_pattern->global_attn_every_n) and exact-erf GeGLU. Tokens now match HF exactly: [50281,25521,1533,50282].
models.measured_note: SHIPPED IS Q8_0 (not q4_k like the other entries). Final-embedding (CLS-pool + L2) cos vs HF sentence-transformers = 0.999602; per-stage q8_0 vs HF fp32 = 0.999928 at the emb_ln_out structural gate and 0.99986-0.99998 across all 22 layers. The residual is quantization: the f16 control (below) is cos=1.000000 at EVERY stage AND 0.999999 final, proving the tokenizer + modern-bert graph (GeGLU-erf, dual-theta RoPE, sliding-window attn) are exact.

models.name: granite-embedding-107m-multilingual
models.query: how do I bake sourdough bread
models.related: A step-by-step guide to baking sourdough loaves at home.
models.unrelated: The 1998 amendment to the municipal zoning ordinance.
models.notes: The FIRST SentencePiece entry in the matrix — an XLM-RoBERTa-family embedder exported as arch 'bert' with tokenizer.ggml.model='t5' (250002-token unigram vocab + scores). Exercises the model-string->SPM dispatch (t5->type 2) added for the modern-bert fix, plus pooling_type=2 (CLS). NOTE it uses absolute position offset 0 (unlike the intfloat multilingual-e5 XLM-R models, which need offset 2 and whose community GGUFs omit bert.position_offset -> those do NOT parity-match; see PLAN).
models.measured_note: q4_k floor. Final-embedding (CLS-pool + L2) cos vs HF sentence-transformers = 0.996145; per-stage q4_k vs HF fp32 = 0.999951 at the emb_ln_out structural gate and 0.9928-0.9969 across all 6 layers. The f16 control (below) is cos=1.000000 at EVERY stage AND 1.000000 final, proving the SPM tokenizer + bert graph are exact and the q4_k gap is quantization.
